title: Limited-Sources Justification Sysmex hematology analyzers
context: [page 1 of TAB D Limited Sources Justification (LSJ) under FAR Part 8.405-6.pdf] CUI Controlled by: Defense Health Agency (DHA) Controlled by: DHACA HCD-C CUI Category(ies): Source Selection Limited Dissemination Control: FED ONLY POC: (Insert POC) CUI Source Selection Information - See FAR 2.101 and 3.104-4 1 Limited Sources Justification (LSJ) Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 8.405-6 1. Identification of the Agency and Contracting Activity: Defense Health Agency (DHA), Healthcare Contracting Division-Central (HCD-C). 2. Nature and/or Description of Action being Approved: This is a request for a sole source to Sysmex Corporation for a follow-on requirement to Contract number FA700020A0015 that expires 30 September 2025. 3. Description of Supplies or Services and Estimated Value: The DHA requires the lease of the Sysmex XN-3100-111 Hematology Analyzer and lease of the Sysmex DI-60 Automated Digital Cell Morphology System and all related and required maintenance and repair, supplies, and consumables for both machines at Evans Army Community Hospital, (EACH), Colorado. The vendor shall provide all required equipment, reagents, parts, control, and maintenance, and calibration materials required for the machine to perform full services. EACH currently leases both of these integrated pieces of equipment: one (1) Sysmex XN-3100-111 Hematology Analyzer and one (1) Sysmex DI-60 Automated Digital Cell Morphology System. Proposed Ordering Vehicle: FSS Contract Number V797D40235 Proposed Vendor: Sysmex America, Inc. 577 Aptakisic Road, Lincolnshire, IL Proposed Contract Type: Firm-Fixed Price Period of Performance: Six-month base period with four (4) one-year option periods The estimated total contract value, including the 4 options is $731,692.26. The firm-fixed- price uses a fixed per month rate. The period of performance will be a six-month base period with four (4) one-year option Period Period of Performance Estimated Value Base Period 1 October 2025 to 31 March 2026 $82,449.54 Option Period 1 01 April 2026 to 31 March 2027 $162,310.68 Option Period 2 01 April 2027 to 31 March 2028 $162,310.68 Option Period 3 01 April 2028 to 31 March 2029 $162,310.68 Option Period 4 01 April 2029 to 31 March 2030 $162,310.6 Total $731,692.26 [page 2 of TAB D Limited Sources Justification (LSJ) under FAR Part 8.405-6.pdf] CUI CUI Source Selection Information - See FAR 2.101 and 3.104-4 2 4. Authority Cited: FAR 8.405-6(a)(1)(i)(B) Only one source is capable of providing the supplies or services required at the level of quality required because the supplies or services are unique or highly specialized. 5. Rationale Justifying Use of Authority Cited: The Sysmex XN-3100-111 Hematology Analyzer is the only analyzer that meets all of EACH’s mission and technical requirements to provide an automated hematology analyzer that can perform laboratory testing and connect to the lab information system. While other analyzers may offer similar basic CBC functionality, the XN-3100-111 possesses specific, essential characteristics vital to the EACH’s mission. All parameters of the Sysmex XN3100's test menu are FDA approved including body fluid two-part differential mononuclear & polynuclear percentage and counts, unique to Sysmex. The Sysmex DI-60 adds complete automation of the manual WBC differential process and can only integrate with the Sysmex Analyzers. The Analyzer requested can only integrate with Sysmex automation products. Combining two vendor products would not meet the requirements because there would be no known probability of test results. Use of Sysmex hematology systems is required to meet the laboratory’s mission needs, as the equipment provides a fully integrated and automated solution. Procuring separate instruments from multiple vendors would result in workflow fragmentation, increased manual interventions, and interface compatibility risks that could compromise testing accuracy, turnaround times, and staff efficiency. A mixed-vendor approach would undermine the continuity of automation, quality control, and data management that are essential for reliable hematology testing in support of patient care. Therefore, Sysmex is the only source that can provide the complete end-to-end automation necessary to meet the laboratory’s operational requirements. The ATO Approved XN-3100-111 is the only automated hematology system pairing one XN10 and one XN20 fully automated hematology analyzers with an integrated SP-50 Slide Maker/Stainer, and an integrated DI-60 Automated Digital Cell Morphology System. The XN-20 module has unique added technology to differentiate between blast and atypical lymph cells. This differentiation is a mission requirement. Automated analyzers not interfaced with the laboratory information system will require manual entry of results, which increases the safety risks of clerical errors. Manual entry of results also requires second verification prior to reporting, which increases the turn-around-time for reporting results to providers and cause delays in patient care. It would also increase commercial lab testing costs and need to cover the gap in the lab’s testing capability. If another analyzer was able to meet EACH’s mission requirements, EACH would still need to establish new processes and procedures to run blood tests, including training on the use of the machine. EACH would also require a new lab configuration for any other potential replacement and may not be able to support the size and processing area for another machine. Sysmex America Inc. is the sole manufacturer of the Sysmex line of hematology analyzers as well as the reagents and supplies used by those systems in the United States. These items are [page 3 of TAB D Limited Sources Justification (LSJ) under FAR Part 8.405-6.pdf] CUI CUI Source Selection Information - See FAR 2.101 and 3.104-4 3 proprietary to Sysmex America Inc. Sysmex service engineers and individuals trained under the Sysmex biomedical engineer training program are trained and specifically certified by Sysmex to service Sysmex equipment. There are no other authorized providers for the service of the Sysmex analyzers. Federal Supply System Contract V797D40235 with Sysmex identifies that Sysmex does have some authorized participating distributors; however, Sysmex does not provide the proprietary information to distributions required to, and does not authorize those distributors to provide, the required maintenance services. Even if a non-Sysmex individual may have the knowledge to perform maintenance, they will not have the right tools to access the latest software updates. No other provider can service or maintain this equipment due to the proprietary nature of the analyzer. A non-authorized servicer/maintainer can also void the warranty of the leased equipment. Furthermore, the required reagents and supplies are only manufactured and provided by Sysmex. Even if there was another source for a machine or supply that met the mission needs, the requirement is for the vendor to also meet in-person technical needs, service response times, and maintenance requirements that would be available to travel to EACH, and not merely provide the items as supply. 6. Market Research: The Government reviewed contracts for the same service awarded by other Government agencies, the Federal Procurement Data System, Federal Supply Schedules, and other sole source justifications posted to SAM.gov Contract Opportunities. There are many sole sources for different locations, some for this company, some for others because each MTF has different requirements and different space allocations. The Government reviewed other potential sources discovered during this research. For requirements very similar to this requirement at Evans Army Community Hospital the Government found many sole sources to Sysmex XN-3100-111 existed. Research also included the open market options through internet and industry website searches. The Government posted a Notice of Intent to Limited Sources by intention to make an award to Sysmex on SAM.gov on 25 April 2025 which closed on 8 May 2025. No questions nor responses were received. This research did not reveal any other company, besides Sysmex, that would meet this MTF’s needs. Additionally, posting requirements under IAW FAR 8.405-6(a)(2) and FAR 5.203(a) will be followed after place the order. This posting may year more market research for future option decisions or future buys. 7. Other Facts: The current ending requirement was awarded as sole source blanket purchase agreement order to Sysmex America, Inc under FA700020A0015. Because that was an Air Force purchase and this is not a DHA requirement, I was not able to gain access to the entire file of prior market research for the current services. However, throughout market research was done and current services were reviewed and confirmed to be acceptable or better. 8. title: Notice of Intent-Sole Source - MSO North Office Expansion
context: [page 1 of Limited Source - MSO North Cubicle Build Out.pdf] LIMITED SOURCE JUSTIFICATION PURSUANT TO FAR 13.106-1 1. CONTRACTING AGENCY: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Seattle District, 4735 East Marginal Way South, Seattle, WA 98134. 2. DESCRIPTION OF ACTION: Approval is requested for a brand-name and single source justification for MillerKnoll furniture to be provided and installed by contractor Business Interiors Northwest to provide, design and install two (2) new cubicles in Mission Support Office – North (MSO-N). 3. DESCRIPTION OF SERVICES: In order to provide adequate space for new employees in support of the Administration’s effort to consolidate office space, two (2) new office cubicles need to be design and built in the MSO-N office space. The total estimated cost for this work is $75,000. 4. AUTHORITY CITED: FAR 13.106-1(b) Soliciting from a single source. (i) For purchases not exceeding the simplified acquisition threshold. 5. REASON FOR AUTHORITY CITED: Pursuant to FAR 13.106-1(b)(1)(i) “Contracting Officers may solicit from one source if the con tracting officer determines that the circumstances of the contract action deem only one source reasonably available (e.g., urgency, exclusive licensing agreements, brand name or industrial mobilization).” Ou r current furniture is custom-made, brand- name MillerKnoll furniture. In order to maintain consistency in aesthetics, only brand-name MillerKnoll furniture must be used. In order maintain our current warranty, any office space furniture and install needs to be done by a MillerKnoll Authorized vendor. 6. BASIS FOR RESTRICTING COMPETITION: The new workspaces that need to be built must match the current aesthetics in fabric, laminate as well as f unctionality and design in order to maintain compatibility with the existing furniture in the MSO-N and co nsistency with all other furniture in the District. Each brand of furniture has certain configurations, f abric colors, texture and style and connection points on their parts which are unique to their own brand. T here are no alternative brand names that are equally compatible and would be able to connect seamlessly and match exactly in aesthetics with the MillerKnoll brand parts and configurations. To use an alternative brand requires having to purchase all new office furniture not only for the MSO-N, but for the entire district office. This is very impractical and cost prohibitive and therefore not an option. Finally, the District has a warranty for all existing furniture in the District, to include the furniture in the MSO-N. This warranty states that only a MillerKnoll authorized vendor must be used to install their furniture. If a MillerKnoll authorized vendor is not used to install the new cubicles, our warranty would be null and voi d, thus unnecessarily eliminating a benefit the Government has. 7. MARKET RESEARCH: Due to the required expedited nature of this requirement, a search was conducted for MillerKnoll Authorized vendors in the Seattle area via Google as well as on GSA as a l ocal vendor will be able to respond quickly. Both searches led to only one (1) vendor, Business Interiors Northwest. A call with MillerKnoll determined that they only have one (1) authorized vendor in the Seattle area, which is Business Interiors Northwest. McMillan DATE: TITLE: Contracting Officer SIGNATURE: 2 [page 1 of PWS - MSO-N Office Build Out.pdf] PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT (PWS) Seattle District Mission Support Office - North Build Out USACE Seattle District, 4735 E. Marginal Way S. Bldg. 1202, Seattle WA 98134 1.0 General Information. 1.1 Background. There is a District-wide reallocation of existing workspaces that requires the Mission Support Officer and one Mission Support Office employee to relocate to new workspaces. New workspaces must match the current aesthetics in fabric, laminate as well as functionality and design. 1.2 Scope of Work. Contractor shall procure and install two (2) cubicles for the Mission Support Office in accordance with Attachment A. Work order shall be all-inclusive to deliver workspaces in turnkey condition, including desk, cabinets, chair, and electrical and communications utility services. 1.3 Period of Performance. The contractor shall complete all work stated in this PWS in its entirety no later than 60 calendar days after receipt of award. 1.4 Quality Control 1.5.1 The contractor shall designate, in writing, an employee who shall serve as the contact for matters involving quality and performance or nonperformance of the required work stated in this PWS . The employee(s) shall be qualified and fully competent with full authority to act for, and on behalf of, the contractor as necessary to ensure that the required work is performed in accordance with the standards contained herein. The contractor shall furnish the above written designation to the Government’s Quality Assurance Representative (QAR) no later than the first day of work. The contractor shall include the name(s), address(s), and telephone number(s) of the responsible individual(s). 1.5.2 The Contracting Officer reserves the right to disapprove any individual whom he considers incompetent to perform the work required. title: Notice of Intent to Sole Source to Mark 43, Inc.
context: [page 1 of 1.9.1 Redacted JA.pdf] Sole Source Justification (SSJ) Simplified Procedures for Certain Commercial items for procurements exceeding the Simplified Acquisition Threshold (SAT) pursuant to FAR Subpart 13.5, including Brand Name Page 1 of 3 Sole Source Justification 1. Agency and Contracting Activity. The Department of Homeland Security (DHS), United States Security Service (USSS), Office of Procurement, proposes to enter into a contract on behalf of Uniformed Division (UD), on a basis other than full and open competition. 2. Nature and/or description of the action being approved. USSS intends to procure on a sole source basis using Simplified Procedures for Certain Commercial Items without seeking competition for the acquisition of FedRAMP Record Management System (RMS) Software as a Service. This action is being taken in pursuant to FAR 13.501. The contract type for the proposed follow-on award to Mark43, Inc. is a firm fixed priced (FFP) contract. USSS intends to establish a 5-year FFP contract to Mark43, Inc. for continuity of services for an exclusive technology focused cloud-based system to facilitate efficient exchange of information with the Washington, D.C. Metropolitan Police Department, and other law enforcement entities in the National Capitol Region (NCR). Vendor Information: Mark 43, Inc. 250 Hudson St., FL 3 New York, NY 10013 UEI No. YLDGC3H3GW43 3. Description of Supplies/Services. This requirement is for a multi-tenant cloud based FedRAMP High Record Management System (RMS) Software as a Service that meets federal standards to include National Incident-Based Reports System (NIBRS) and Criminal Justice Information Services (CJIS). The RMS provides the capabilities for users to generate inquiries to internal and external data sources—such as state Department of Motor Vehicles and criminal history files, as well as the National Crime Information Center (NCIC). The RMS provides for the storage, retrieval, retention, manipulation, archiving, and viewing of information, records, documents, or files pertaining to law enforcement operations. RMS covers the entire life span of records development, from the initial generation to its completion. For the purposes of this document, RMS is limited to records directly related to law enforcement operations. Such records include incident and accident reports, arrests, citations, warrants, case management, field contacts, and other operations- oriented records. 4. Identification of the authority. ☒ 41 U.S.C. 1901, using SAP up to $7.5M as authorized by FAR 13.500(a) and implemented by FAR 13.501(a). 5. Demonstration that the proposed contractor’s unique qualifications or the nature of the acquisition requires use of the authority cited. [page 2 of 1.9.1 Redacted JA.pdf] Sole Source Justification (SSJ) Simplified Procedures for Certain Commercial items for procurements exceeding the Simplified Acquisition Threshold (SAT) pursuant to FAR Subpart 13.5, including Brand Name Page 2 of 3 Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements: Mark43, Inc. is the only source capable of providing the software services at the level of quality required to satisfy the agency’s requirements. Mark43 RMS is the only cloud-based records system used by partner law enforcement agencies such as Metropolitan Police Department, Park Police, and Capitol Police and is currently in use by the USSS Uniformed Division (UD). Additionally, Mark43 RMS has been identified as the only vendor capable of providing USSS UD with consolidated analytical threat reports generated from its proprietary database and have the ability to interface with the local police department. This information is needed to make immediate threat level determinations and actions associated with adverse information against UD personnel. Other sources researched lacked the capacity and access to key proprietary or public databases such as the real-time arrest and incarceration records database maintained by the local police department. While other sources were identified capable of providing equivalent services and is FedRAMP High certified, their system lacks the interoperability needed for a constant back and forth communication flow between agencies using the Mark43 RMS platform. Information collected by USSS needs to be shared among other federal agencies such as the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) and the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), United States Park Police (USPP), United States Capital Police (USCP), Metropolitan Police Department (MPD). This information needs to be accurate with immediate availability, back-up system and technical support 24/7 to help eliminate risks associated with national security. 6. Description of efforts made to ensure that offers are solicited from as many potential sources as is practicable, including whether a notice was or will be publicized as required by FAR Subpart 5.2 and, if not, which exception under FAR 5.202 applies. As required by the Small Business Act (15 U.S.C. 637(e) and the Office of Federal Procurement Policy Act (41 U.S.C. 1708), a notice of intent to sole source to Mark43, Inc. will be posted on SAM.gov in accordance with FAR 5.2. The estimated date of publication is 17 February 2025. 7. Determination by the contracting officer that the anticipated cost to the Government will be fair and reasonable. FAR 13.106-3(a)(2)(i) states that for the basis for award, “The contracting officer may base the statement on “comparison of the proposed price with prices found reasonable on previous purchases.” 8. Description of market research. Market research was conducted via internet searches, consulting subject matter experts from various agencies with similar requirements and posting a Request for Information (RFI) to identify any new vendors that have technology equivalent to or exceeds Mark43 legacy systems used by most Police agencies in the National Capital Region. [page 3 of 1.9.1 Redacted JA.pdf] Sole Source Justification (SSJ) Simplified Procedures for Certain Commercial items for procurements exceeding the Simplified Acquisition Threshold (SAT) pursuant to FAR Subpart 13.5, including Brand Name Page 3 of 3 A review was also done of existing Department of Homeland Security strategic sourcing vehicles (SSVs) to see if any systems are available. Vendor engagement meetings revealed that existing platforms could be modified to match the requirement but could not be linked with legacy systems, such as Mark43 used in the NCR to exchange information. Additionally, Request for Information (RFI) 70US0924R700942672 was drafted and posted on SAM.gov on 8 March 2024 inviting vendors to provide an overview of their products and services to meet the agency’s needs. While there were several vendors that expressed interest and provided a capabilities statement, most lacked Authority to Operate (ATO) within DHS network or other systems and/or Federal Risk and Authorization Management Program (FedRAMP) Approval, providing a standardized approach to security for cloud-based products and services. With Mark43 being a legacy system in the National Capital Region currently in use by the Metropolitan Police Department DC, Park Police, and Capital Police, vendors who responded lacked the interoperability to communicate with existing Mark43 users, making them unable to meet the agency’s needs. 9. Any other facts supporting the justification. N/A 10. A listing of the sources, if any that expressed, in writing, an interest in the acquisition. In an effort to update Market Research, RFI 70US0924R70094272 was posted on SAM.gov on 8 March 2024 and closed on 7 April 2024 to identify industry capabilities. After extensive review, only some of the vendors were currently FedRAMP high certified. Per the RFI “The offeror shall provide all resources and support to stand-up the solution in a FedRAMP approved High Cloud production, development, and training environment.” Additionally, the RFI stated “The proposed RMS must be a complete multi-tenant cloud based FedRAMP High service ready for immediate use” and that the system shall allow USSS to “shared among other federal agencies such as the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) and the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), United States Park Police (USPP), United States Capital Police (USCP), Metropolitan Police Department (MPD).” An email was sent to each RFI respondent to verify current interface capabilities. The Metropolitan Police Department, Park Police and Capitol Police currently use Mark43 RMS and there are no other systems capable of communicating with Mark43 RMS at this time. 11. title: N4 ERP+ Support
context: [page 1 of JEFO N4 ERP Support-Redacted.pdf] Source Selection Information – See FAR 2.101 and 3.104 Document # 26-185 JUSTIFICATION FOR AN EXCEPTION TO FAIR OPPORTUNITY (ABOVE SAT) 1. Identification of Requiring Activity and Contracting Activity. The requiring activity is the Assistant Secretary of the Navy, Financial Management & Comptroller (ASN (FM&C)), Washington, DC. The contracting activity is NAVSUP Fleet Logistics Center (FLC) Norfolk, Contracting Dept., BUMED/FM&C Directorate. 2. Nature and description of contract action. This acquisition is conducted under the authority of 10 U.S.C. 3406(c)(5). This action is an exception to the fair opportunity process to be awarded as a modification to an existing task order. The placement of a new Cost-Plus Fixed Fee (CPFF) CLIN on an existing order is anticipated. This procurement action is to modify the fleet migration support services currently performed by Deloitte and Touche LLP under Contract N0018922DZ017, Task Order N0018925FZ224, which was solicited on a competitive basis but ultimately received only one quote. This justification specifically addresses the requirements to expand analysis and support to OPNAV N4. 3. Description of Required Supplies/Services to meet the agency’s needs. The proposed acquisition is to issue a modification to an existing Task Order issued to Deloitte. Task order N0018925FZ224 provides functional support services assisting in the generation, design, and implementation of requirements supporting the Navy’s technical upgrade of the Navy ERP system from ERP Central Component (ECC) to S/4 HANA. This technical upgrade is a critical part of a holistic effort called ERP+ to modernize the Navy’s financial management IT infrastructure and operations. The current instance of Navy ERP (ECC) is approaching obsolescence and its software will no longer be supported by its manufacturer. ERP+ is targeting deployment starting in FY29 to ensure the continued availability of a modern ERP that will drive the Navy’s ability to sustain a clean audit opinion year-over-year. The original scoping of ERP+ was on the Navy’s financial management (FM) community. During the course of performance on the current contract, the government made the design decisions to include Navy Operational Supply System (NOSS) requirements in ERP+. After analyzing 3,500 NOSS requirements, it was determined that ERP+ covered ~88%, which made the ERP+ S/4HANA platform the best path forward. A Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) was signed in October 2025 between OASN (FM&C) and OPNAV N4 to deliver operational supply capability via ERP+. This task order modification would provide contractor support for [page 2 of JEFO N4 ERP Support-Redacted.pdf] Source Selection Information – See FAR 2.101 and 3.104 ERP+-related services similar to what is being provided for FM to the OPNAV N4 logistics community in order to pave the way for NOSS requirements to be delivered through ERP+. Specifically, the proposed tasks would provide 1) LOG IT Governance, 2) IT Portfolio Management, 3) Resource and Financial (POM) analysis, and 4) Requirements Analysis. Without additional support to N4, there is an increased likelihood that these efforts may fail to achieve their necessary milestones on the timelines required to meet the DON’s ERP+ timeline, putting at risk the Navy’s ability to sustain a clean audit and successfully integrate NOSS. Specific services and key goals of the proposed task order are: LOG IT Governance to manage, analyze, and provide recommendations based on strategic N4 leadership direction, agenda development, briefing material, leadership talking points, coordination with external stakeholders, meeting minutes, action tracking, and overall governance preparation, scheduling, and battle rhythm. IT Portfolio Management to manage, analyze, and provide recommendations for LOG IT systems, applications, capabilities alignment to the BEA and capabilities requirements documents and the overall roadmap for LOG IT modernization and cattle-drive in-service LOG IT systems. Includes support for using and analyzing authoritative LOG IT system data and interface standards. Resource and Financial (POM) analysis to manage, analyze, and provide recommendations for the N4L6 Logistics and Warfighting POM balance based on OSW, DON, Navy and N4L6 priorities. Includes analyzing historical financial data, managing obligations and expenditures, and reviewing reports daily, cost estimates and other artifacts to determine funded and unfunded priorities. Requirements Analysis to manage, analyze, and provide recommendations for generating and documenting requirements, and managing end-to-end logistics processes, supporting the development of capability needs statements via DoDI 8000.57 (Software Acquisition Pathway), supporting and managing integrated product teams and associated outputs to gather, document, and analyze requirements and their delivery to support LOG IT implementation The period of performance for N4 LOG IT Support is seven (7) months. The Government Estimate for N4L6 LOG IT Support is . This modification is estimated to increase the value of task order N0018925FZ224 from to , a increase. 4. Identification of the Exception to Fair Opportunity and Supporting Rationale - Including Demonstration of Contractor’s Unique Qualifications. The statutory authority that permits not providing each awardee a fair opportunity to be considered for each order exceeding the micro-purchase threshold issued under a multiple award contract is 10 U.S.C. 3406(c)(5), as implemented by FAR 16.507-6(b). The applicable exception to the fair opportunity process for this justification for the award of an order exceeding the simplified acquisition threshold is: [page 3 of JEFO N4 ERP Support-Redacted.pdf] Source Selection Information – See FAR 2.101 and 3.104 The exception to the fair opportunity process is FAR 16.507-6(b)(2), Only one awardee is capable of providing the supplies or services required at the level of quality required because the supplies or services ordered are unique or highly specialized. Deloitte was awarded the ERP+ Requirements Generation TO (N0018924FZ713) in 2024. This task order was solicited as a competitive task order on the FIP IV vehicle, and Deloitte was found to be the only offeror that submitted an at least acceptable technical proposal. Likewise, Deloitte was awarded the follow-on effort (N0018925FZ224) in August 2025 as the only offeror that submitted a proposal. Deloitte demonstrated a complete background in Government-specific financial system knowledge and DON business/operation processes. Deloitte was the only firm that demonstrated the capability to deploy a fully qualified workforce (including key personnel) on the timelines required to achieve the task order’s goals. Starting with the performance of N0018924FZ713, Deloitte gained invaluable institutional knowledge as it assisted the DON with undertaking a critical multi-year transformation to modernize financial management, logistics, supply chain, and other core business functions through a complex technical upgrade . During course of the performance of N0018925FZ224, the government made a design decision to incorporate NOSS requirements into ERP+. While this has long-term ramifications for the overall ERP+ project, the most immediate impact is that strategic support to Governance, Portfolio Management, Requirements Analysis, and financial analysis is needed now to lay the groundwork for this transition. This support needs to be integrated with current ERP+ support underway with the FM community because it is essentially the same project: designing, generating, and implementing requirements for the ERP+ platform. The increase in scope to encompass logistics is a logical extension of the current services. The incorporation of LOG IT Governance, IT Portfolio Management, Resource and Financial (POM) Analysis, and Requirements Analysis into the existing Performance Work Statement (PWS) is critical to establishing momentum for the N4 ERP+ transition. As the current performer, Deloitte possesses specialized understanding of the Department of the Navy's (DON) business processes, systems, and strategic ERP+ objectives. Awarding these specific N4 tasks to Deloitte directly leverages their ongoing expertise and execution of the core task order tasks already being performed for the FM community. Deloitte is already managing governance, aligning technical capabilities, and supporting cross-functional Integrated Product Teams (IPTs) for system requirements development. Additionally, Deloitte has existing, cleared staff that are ready to commence work immediately on contract and do not require suitability processing. Transitioning these tightly coupled N4 logistics and IT portfolio tasks to a secondary vendor would introduce significant integration risks, duplicate foundational efforts, and cause unacceptable schedule delays.
